articleTitle: Development of low dielectric constant pressboard
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: High breakdown strengths of oil-impregnated insulating materials are expected and the insulating design is improved if the dielectric constant of cellulose material is close to that of insulating oil. This paper presents a low dielectric constant pressboard which can be obtained by blending polymethylpentene fibre with cellulose fibre. The dielectric constant is 3.5, which is a very low value compared with the 4.7 of conventional pressboard. By using the new pressboard, decreased insulating distances and smaller transformer sizes are expected.

articleTitle: Testing and measurement techniques for the evaluation of organic insulating materials for hv outdoor application
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: Organic materials, especially with fibre reinforcement, are of increasing importance for HV outdoor application. Since polymers normally are more sensitive against weathering than porcelain, it is important to test the withstand capability of such materials and to evaluate their resistivity. Special attention must be paid to the phenomena of erosion and water absorption. Test pro cedures and results are reported. It can be demonstrated that water repellent materials exhibit superior properties.

articleTitle: On the regularity of the branching structure of electrical trees
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: The spatial pattern formation of the electrical tree in PMMA and PC samples has been investigated using impulse voltages. Moreover, the pattern of the electrical tree produced by com puter simulation has been analyzed. The results show that the regularity of branches of electrical tree conforms to Horton's law. Also, the fractal properties of electrical tree will be described from the point of view of fractal dimension.

articleTitle: A comparative study on sensitivity analysis of various open-ended coaxial line geometries
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: An open-ended coaxial line can be used as a non-destructive broad band impedance sensor to measure the permittivity of various liquids. This paper presents a sensitivity analysis on permittivity measure ments for open-ended coaxial lines with different extremity bevelling angles.

articleTitle: DC characteristics of cable insulating materials (part 1)
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: DC characteristics of cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) are influenced by peroxide decomposition products and antioxidants. The former increases space charge accumulation and decreases volume resistivity, while the latter increases space charge accumulation. DC breakdown strength of a lowdensity polyethylene (LDPE) cable without additives is higher than that of a XLPE cable.

articleTitle: Early stages in dielectric ageing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: We attempt to give a systematic survey from a solid state physics point of view of the relevant electronic, chemical and electrochemical processes in the early stages of dielectric ageing. A first conclusion is that no ageing occurs as long as the dielectric behaves as a dielectric. Ageing always involves a flow of current which by various mechanisms e.g. heating, chemical damage by hot electrons, electrochemical reactions at interfaces weakens the material which then in combination with mechanical and electromechanical forces leads to damage. The crucial processes which have to be understood are the charge flow at points of high local field enhancement and at interfaces and the damage mechanisms resulting from charge flow.

articleTitle: Electrical insulation and its future
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: Insulation engineering has progressed rapidly, especially since the 1940's, under continuous input and advances from the development of polymer technology along with the evolution of material engineering and electric power technology. Now, in the late 1980's, it is felt that the field of electric insulation engineering has almost reached maturation.

articleTitle: The structure of additives and their relation to streaming current
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: When a liquid with good insulating properties is set in flow electrification will occur. The charge produced may cause various static electricity problems for the chemical industry or destroy the insulating systems of the very-high-voltage transformers used in electrical engineering. Measures taken to prevent this kind of mishap include reduction in liquid flow velocity, the use of liquids with low electrification properties and the introduction of anti-electrification additives. In very-high-voltage transformers, a reduction in the oil flow velocity leads to a lowering of the cooling efficiency, so that the transformer has to be made very large. The use of low electrification oils. on the other hand, adds to the cost of operation. In such cases, the most effective and economical means of preventing electrification would seem to be the use of additives. However, bearing in mind the need to prevent pollution and to ensure that no deterioration occurs in the anti-electrification system with age. we find that a number of unresolved problems still remain. The authors have been engaged in experiments to find interface activating substances that are inexpensive, safe and highly effective in reducing electrification. Their results have led them to conclude that the use of nonionic agents is more effective in all kinds of circumstances than the use of ionic agents. They have conducted further experiments using interface activation additives of differing molecular structures in order to determine which structure works most effectively against electrification. The present experiment concerns only two types of additives. those with an alkyl base and those with a phenol base. It was found that the phenol based additives are more ef fective in reducing electrification.

articleTitle: Development of 22 kv very low-frequency, high-voltage generator and the characteristics of partial discharge in XLPE cables
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: For diagnosis of power cables, direct current voltage has presently been used in tests. Direct current voltage is, however, not always effective, especially in measuring the partial discharge characteristics of XLPE cables. The weak point of testing when used with power frequency voltage is that it requires a very weighty transformer. We chose a very low frequency voltage as a power source in place of the direct current, and made a 22kV high-voltage generator with very low frequency (0.1Hz). We carried out tests on the characteristics of the partial discharge in XLPE cables and confirmed that the very low frequency method can induce partial discharge with characteristics approximately identical to that of the power frequency source.

articleTitle: Study of main insulation structure in 10,35kv power transformer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: 10,35KV power transformers (PT) are the most prodnets in tra nsformer factories in our country. Rationaly selecting main in sulation structures (MIS) and sizes of 10,35KV PT will be more economical and scientific for our industry of PT. This paper gave the internal negularity of MIS in 10,35KV PT through simulation test of conducting-paper and numerical calculation for electric field around winding end and breakdown test of the model. Based on the results, the sizes of MIS in 10,35KV PTwere defined which satisfied voltage test standard in China.

articleTitle: Measurements on the frozen strain in XLPE insulated cables using thermo mechanical analysis
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: This study is presented on the frozen strain in XLPE measured by means of a thermomechanical analysis (TMA). The magnitude of the strain in XLPE insu lated cables ranges from 2 to 8 % and the cable insulation is stressed in tension for the axial and azimuthal directions and compression for the radial direction. Thermomechanical properties of XLPE are also measured, which are indispensable to evaluate strain distribution.

articleTitle: Developmetn of transformer insulation utilizing new low-permitivity pressboards
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: A pressboard providing both low permittivity and good mechanical properties is required as for insulating material in oil-immersed transformers insulation. Using a newly developed pressboard, insulation characteristics of intercoil models are investigated under lightning impulses and AC voltage conditions. it is demonstrated that a spacer fabricated from the new pressboard material (permittivity of 3.5) increases the partial discharge inception and breakdown voltages up to 30%, compared with those of conventional pressboard spacers (permittivity of 4.7).

articleTitle: Diffusion of ions into polymers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: Not only have ionic solutions been used to initiate water treeing in polyethylene under laboratory conditions, but evidence has been obtained that ions enhance the absorption of water into polyethylene [1] and also enhance the growth of water trees [2, 3, 4, 5]. It has also been shown that ions are present in the treed region of the polymers [6]. Given and Crichton [7, 4] have shown that there is an inverse relationship between the growth rate of trees and the ionic radius on the anion. Given et al. [7] also suggest that the penetration of ions into the polymer will distort its structure by forcing apart the polymer chains in the amorphous region. This in turn is seen as a mechanism for en hancing the rate of water migration into the polymer where the water is held in part by the hydration sphere around the anion. In a cable, the insulating polyethylene is surrounded by a semiconducting jacket. If ions are going to penetrate into the polyethylene insulation, it must first diffuse through the semiconducting jacket and traverse the interface between the semicon and insulation before diffusing into the polyethylene. This paper will describe the experiments designed to study the diffusion of ions through the semicon.

articleTitle: Cross-linking reaction of LDPE and the behavior of decomposition products from cross-linking agents
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: Cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) insulated power cables may occasionally be exposed to high temperatures above 150/spl deg/C for relatively short periods of time. Numerous microvoids are sometimes observed in the XLPE heated under such con ditions. Studies were carried out to clarify the mechanism of this void forma tion in the XLPE insulation. A series of experiments revealed that void for mation. was caused by water generation in the XLPE because of the dehydration of cumyl alcohol produced from the cross-linking agent (dicumyl peroxide: DCP). This reaction may produce /spl alpha/-methylstyrene simultaneously with water. The generation of water was evidently catalyzed by acidic antioxidants while the dehydration was suppressed using certain antioxidants which possessed weak H/sup +/ donating properties.

articleTitle: Measurement of high field AC conduction current in polymeric insulating materials
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: A new method for the measurement of high field ac conduction current in polymeric insulating materials is developed by using an unbalanced operation of the current comparator type high field tan /spl delta/ - capacitance bridge and the deconvolution technique. The new method was checked by the known input signal to the bridge. Finally this technique was applied to the ac conduction in low-density polyethylene films.

articleTitle: Effect of atomic oxygen on polymers used as surface materials for spacecrafts
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: The degradation behavior of polymeric materials due to atomic oxygen was examined under the exposure of oxygen plasma. It was clarified that the mechanism of thickness loss for Kapton was different from that for Teflon. The condition which could simulate the results of flight experiments fairly well was found.

articleTitle: Partial discharges, streamers and trees in condensed matter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: Both partial discharges and streamers have been studied in detail but no connection has been established between the two phenomena. In the present paper such a connection is established and it is shown that streamers are the most probable location of partial discharges. In solid dielectrics, imperfections at the metal/dielectric interface might also contribute to the observed partial discharge channels. The significance of these observations is discussed in detail.

articleTitle: Prebreakdown current and breakdown of polymeric insulating materials
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: Measurements of electrical breakdown, high-field conduction current and prebreakdown current were made on various kinds of polymeric insulating films. The experimental results on electrical breakdown and conduction in dicated that the electrical breakdown is thermal in nature for all kinds of samples. Conditions for observing the sharp current rise just before breakdown, expected to be direct experimental evidence of thermal breakdown, were also studied. It was suggested that the melting point of the sample is closely related to the probability of observing the sharp rise of prebreakdown current.

articleTitle: Improvement in A.C. dielectric breakdown strength of XLPE power cables through diffusing of an additive into the insulation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: In order to halve the insulation thickness of extra-high-voltage XLPE power cables, verification of methods which improve the dielectric performance through the modification of the semiconducting layer is in progress. As part of these efforts, an additive which was found to be most effective by preliminary experiments was added to the semiconducting layer at various concentrations from 0 to 5% on disc specimens. These specimens were then subjected to A. C. dielectric breakdown tests. The analysis of the Weibull distributions of the breakdown strengths revealed that these breakdown strengths were considerably improved at concentrations from 3 to 5 %. In particular, the 10% Weibull breakdown strength was improved by 50%. Furthermore, the insulation of the specimens were subjected to physical and chemical analyses. It was found that a layer diffused with the additive is formed in the insulation in close proportion to the concentration of the additive, and that the density of the amorphous portion in the insulation increases with its formation.

articleTitle: Dependence of an applied DC voltage on electric field distribution in insulating oil using the Kerr-effect technique
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: A modified Kerr electrooptic effect technique has been applied to the direct measurement of electric field strength in dielectric liquids such as transformer oil. In particular, by utilizing the incident elliptically polarized laser beam and modulating the applied DC voltage, it was possible to measure the low electric field for a small Kerr constant in liquids. The time evolution of the electric field distribution was also measured. The nonuniformity of an electric field increased with a rise in time.

articleTitle: Microvoid formation and water generation in cross-linked polyethylene resulting from heat treatment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: In this study, the behavior of water and microvoid formation in heat treated XLPE insulation was investigated. When XLPE is heated, water is generated from cumyl alcohol, a decomposition product of DCP. The water generation is intensified by the antioxidant agent contained in XLPE and the oxygen in the air. The water generation leads to the formation of microvoids in XLPE. After the heat treatment, XLPE becomes supersaturated with moisture resulting in moisture condensation and microvoid formation during the cooling process.

articleTitle: Investigation of insulating materials for DC cables (part 3)
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: The DC breakdown characteristics of various polymers were evaluated using sheet as insulating materials for a HVDC cable. As a result of this evalu ation, modified PE, which was produced by introducing a small amount of a polar group into HDPE, was selected as a promising material. The improvement of the DC characteristics of modified PE was estimated, as shown below, by comparison between the space charge characteristic by means of a thermally stimulated current(TSC) and the DC and impulse breakdown characteristics of LDPE, HDPE, XLPE and modified PE.

articleTitle: Probing of space charge in polar polymers by thermal pulse current technique
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials

articleTitle: Dielectric breakdown of a ceramic-epoxy resin interface on a high voltage ceramic capacitor
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: The dielectric breakdown characteristics of a high voltage ceramic capacitor molded from or coated by epoxy resin have been investigated. Tn particular, breakdown phenomena at the ceramic-epoxy (C-E) interface were concentrated one. Tn such samples, breakdown at the C-E interface did not always occur.

articleTitle: Expert systems of electrical insulation for high-voltage rotating machines
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: In this paper, we discuss applications of expert systems to electrical insulation technology. After comparison of each insulation problem in the knowledge structure, we present an example of a prototyped expert system: an off-line diagnosis system of high voltage motor insulation. The system was created on a Prolog machine, MELCOM PSI-2. This system is easily manipulated in the computer environment "knowledge media station" which enables insulation experts to elaborate their own systems without detailed knowledge of the expert systems.

articleTitle: Effect of dipolar polarization on electrical conduction in polar polymers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: The conduction phenomena of polar polymers were explained by a simple one-carrier model in which effects of dipole orientation were included. Comparing the experimental and calculated current-time (J-t) characteristics, the dipole relaxation time T and the lower limit of car rier mobility /spl mu/ of uniaxially-stretched /spl Beta/-phase polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) were roughly estimated at 26 sec and 3xx10/sup -12/ m/sup 2//Vs, respectively, under the field in the range of 10/sup 6/ to 10/sup 7/ V/m at 353 K.

articleTitle: Autoseparation of thermally stimulated currents and exact estimation of energy depths of their carrier traps
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: A new important concept which enables one to separate observed TSC curves automatically and estimate energy depths of carrier traps from the separated TSC curves by computer has been reported. In this proposal, our asymptotic estimation method, which can estimate the energy depth of the carrier trap exactly and simply, also enables one to characterize self-convergence by the repetition of the computer simulation processes.

articleTitle: Impulse and AC breakdowns of Ln/sub 2/ in the presence of thermally induced bubbles
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: In any practical superconducting system, thermally induced bubbles appear during the process of quenching or cryogenic stabilization. Under these conditions, a high voltage is produced. It is therefore necessary to evaluate the dielectric strength of a coolant in the presence of thermally induced -bubbles. Hara et al./sup (1)-(3)/ investigated the dc breakdown performance of liquid helium and nitrogen under such conditions from the viewpoint of insulation designs of superconducting magnet coils. Here, this paper reports the results of an experimental study on the impulse and ac breakdown characteristics of liquid nitrogen under the condition of thermal bubbling.

articleTitle: Voltage life characteristics of XLPE
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: Voltage life characteristics of XLPE were studied using sheet samples containing artificial impurities. To imitate cable insulation, these samples were made under almost the same condition as actual cables and the sizes of the impurities contained are near those contained in cables. The influence of the sizes or kinds of impurities and the temperature for long-term insulation properties were examined.

articleTitle: A behaviour of trapped carrier excited by different wavelengths of illumination
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: A thermally stimulated current has been observed in anthracene single crys tal of organic material. The specimen was excited at various temperatures by laser light with different wavelengths of 2.08 eV, 2.33 eV and 1.79 eV. As the illumination temperature rises, several orders of decrease in the escape frequency factor v of a carrier trap have been confirmed through exact estimation of the energy depth.

articleTitle: Development of cross-linked polyethylene insulated superconducting cable
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: A superconducting power cable which has a structure similar to the conventional extruded crpss-linked polyethylene cable was proposed and the resulting laboratory size cable has been tested. The prominent features of the design are to exploit the excellent electrical properties of polyethylene in the cryogenic temperatures and to separate the helium coolant from the electrical insulation. The cooling test down to the liquid helium temperature and the voltage test at the liquid nitrogen temperature have been carried out with fair success.

articleTitle: The influence of morphology on electrical tree initiation in polyethylene
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: AC and impulse voltages were applied to needle electrode specimens modelling the interface of the semiconducting layer of the XLPE cable. TEM (transmission electron microscope) photographs of minute electrical trees (not longer than 10 am) immediately after their initiation were examined in detail to clarify the influence of morphology on tree initiation.

articleTitle: Effect of plasma polymer surface layer on the space charge formation in polyethylene
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: In Our Previous Paper(1), We Reported That A Plasma-polymer Surface Layer Deposited On A Polyethylene Film Suppresses Electron Injection Into Polyethylene. The Present Paper Reports The Influence Of Polar Groups Existing In The Plasma Polymer On The Injection-suppressing Effect.

articleTitle: Smoke-generating properties of flame-retardant cables
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: The smoke-generating properties of flame-retardant Cables were evaluated Using a 3m cube test. (1) The smoke density of halogen-containing flameretardant cables is large. (2) The effects of size and jacketing materials are manifested in the 3m cube test. (3) For halogen-free cables, no strong correlation was observed between the results of the 3m cube and NBS tests.

articleTitle: Investigation of noise in discharge phenomena for tracking deterioration
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: This paper discusses the investigation of noise in discharge phenomena for a tracking test of organic insulating materials by means of the IEC 587 test method. Two types of samples were used in this test, ethylene-propylene rubber and polyvinyl chloride. The electric intensity of noise differed among the types of discharge phenomena for the sample surface. Moreover, the electric intensity of noise was effected by the type of sample. Thus, using the above-mentioned method, it was found that the propagation of deterioration on the sample surface progressed in accordance with the increase in the noise intensity.

articleTitle: Localized heat generation in polyethylene films and its relation to dielectric breakdown and high field conduction
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: The localized Joule heating in polyethylene films was detected at room temperature before the dielectric breakdown under dc field. When a high temperature point appeared, the conduction current increased with time. The final breakdown occurred at the point of highest temperature. This good correlation between the breakdown point and the Joule heating point shows that a thermal process takes part in the dc electrical breakdown of polyethylene films at room temperature and that there are weak points for the breakdown in the film where the current density is higher than average.

articleTitle: Thermal aging of polyethylene terephthalate film in SF6
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: The thermal degradation process of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) film in SF6 gas was investigated. At heating temperatures below 120/spl deg/ C, the PET film almost retained initial characteristics. At 140/spl deg/C, the film showed significant changes in mechanical properties. Analysis using various testing apparatuses disclosed that the mechanical strength of PET film had a close relationship with changes in mean molecular weight, glass transition temperature, and crystallization starting temperature.

articleTitle: Electrical conduction of oil/polymer composite
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: The current in diarylethane/PP system was strongly enhanced by the existence of diarylethane. It was larger by several orders of magnitude than that in PP without diarylethane. Its polarity effect was contrary to that of diarylethane/FEF. These differences between FEP and PP were explained by the difference in oil/polymer interaction and the electronegativity of F atoms.

articleTitle: Diagnosis of the aged XLPE cable using frequency and temperature characteristics of tan /spl delta/ II
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials

articleTitle: Carrier traps in ethylene-styrene copolymer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: Carrier traps in ethylene-styrene copolymers were studied by various conduction methods. A model for the trap distribution is presented.

articleTitle: From a simple transformation to a degradation of polymers in contact with a cold plasma
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: Plasma treatments are presented as a too] of transformation. Several examples of treated polymers are given and due to physical methods, a limit between transformation and degradation is shown. The first results of an experimental simulation are given, the aim being to show the best conjunction of species leading to the same result as in the case of a cold plasma.

articleTitle: Spark breakdown in point-sphere air gap inserted with PP film
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: This paper describes the spark breakdown in a point-sphere air gap inserted with PP film subjected to a linearly rising dc voltage. No appreciable polarity effect on the breakdown voltage of the composite was observed at any position of the film. The spark breakdown voltage Y6 increased with increasing the distance of the film position from the sphere electrode x to a critical position x. of about half of a gap distance d, at which it dropped suddenly, then increased again with increasing x to d. In the region of I<I/sub c/, a spark breakdown occured after discharges between the film and the sphere electrode took place repeatedly, while apparently spontaneous spark breakdown occurred in I>I/sub x/. The breakdown mechanism for both regions was discussed.

articleTitle: Preparation of polyimide films by vapor deposition polymerization and their photocurrents
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: Polymerization by vapor deposition using a co-evaporation of the dianhydride and diamine monomers has been investigated for preparation of polyamic acid as a precursor for polyimide films. It was found that the substrate temperature is an important factor in obtaining polyamic acids films containing little amount of residual monomers. Various combinations of different monomers were also studied. It was necessary for the growth of the film that the monomers are reactive to a certain extent. The photocurrent of the vapor deposition polymerized film was larger than that of Kapton film, suggesting that the molecular order differed from those prepared with the solution polymerization.

articleTitle: Charge injbction and electroluminescence threshold field in polymmic material under prebreakdown a.c. field
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: Luminescence and space charge injection have been reported to occur during long-term degradation of polymeric materials under a prebreakdown field /1-3/. The nain hypothesis, concerning the deterioration mechanisms of the lattice, in volves hot electrons processes and/or photodegradation resulting from absorption of recombination-generated UV radiation. In this context, one challenge is to study the correlation between electroluminescence and charge injection. We pre sent, in the following, two very sensitive detection setups, allowing the determi nation of the electric threshold field of these phenouiena. Results are presen ted for two dielectric materials : polyethylene and epoxy resin.

articleTitle: Effect of some additives on the grain resistivity of zinc oxide ceramics
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: The role of the additives, Al/sub 2/O/sub 3/ and Co/sub 2/O/sub 3/ in the conduction mechanism of the ZnO grain, is studied in this paper. The resistivity of sintered, undoped pellets decreases significantly with increasing temperature, and with do ping additives Al/sub 2/O/sub 3/ and Co/sub 2/O/sub 3/ (in moderate amounts). Decreasing resistivity with doping Al/sub 2/O/sub 3/ is due to increasing the carrier density, and decreasing resistivity with doping Co/sub 2/O/sub 3/ is due to changing the grain sub-boun dary microstructure of ZnO grains. The sub-boundary microstructure of ZnO grains with the additive Co/sub 2/O/sub 3/ (<0.5 mol%) is more compact than that without it, so that carriers in it have larger mobility.

articleTitle: Preparation of polypyrrole by GVD method and its electrical properties
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: Polypyrrole film was prepared using iodine vapor. Spectroscopic measurements showed that the polypyrrole films had a chain structure of not only pyrrole units but also some saturated pyrrolidine units or partially saturated units and hydroxyl groups. The polypyrrole film had a conductivity of 10/sup -1/ (S/cm). The temperature dependence of its conductivity was similar to that of electrochemically prepared polypyrrole.

articleTitle: Electrical properties of TiO/sub 2/ thin film prepared by sol-gel method
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: TiO/sub 2/ thin films were prepared by the sol-gel method using the metal alkoxides ( Ti (0-i-Pr)/sub 4/ tetra isopropoxi titanium; TIPT). These films crystalline form was changed by the prepared sol condition and the heat treatment temperature. When the ratio (r) of H/sub 2/O to TIPT is 7, the crystalline form is assumed at 400/spl deg/C. On the other hand, the condition for r=1 was at 500/spl deg/C. For both r=1 and 7, the crystalline form was anatase. It was found that the electrical properties of TiO/sub 2/ film became semiconductive with increasing heat treatment temperature.

articleTitle: Pre-breakdown phenomena and breakdown in gas-insulated systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: The influence of the voltage form and voltage application duration in particle free and particle contaminated GIS on the pre-breakdown phase and the breakdown was examined at different gas pressures. The results refer to events initiated at both the electrode-gas and the insulator-gas interfaces and they are obtained by using both realistic and scaled gas-insulated systems.

articleTitle: Investigation of a monolayer at the air/water interface using a current-measuring technique
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: There has been much interest in the behavior of constituent molecules of a monolayer at the air/water interface. In the present paper, we developed a current-measuring technique to re place the conventional surface potential method. Using this technique, we have investigated the physical properties of fatty acid monolayers at the air/ water interface and determined the dipole moment of the acids.

articleTitle: Intercalation and electrical properties of graphite fibers with thermal and air stability
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: Vapor-grown carbon fibers have been obtained by pyrolysis of hydrocarbons, such as benzene and methane, by a catalytic effect of ultrafine metal particles(i). Two different methods, have been developed for successful formation of the fibers, the substrate method and the aerogel system(1)(2)(3).By the substrate method, thick(/spl tilde/10/spl mu/m diameter) and long fibers(/spl tilde/20cm long) can be grown. By the aerogel system, where the catalytic particles are floating in the reaction chamber, very thin fibers of less than 1/spl mu/m in diameter and less than several mm in length have been effectively produced. From gas phase, these carbon fibers have a high degree of preferred orientation and exhibit a high degree of graphitizability high enough for intercalation. The intercalated vapor-grown carbon fibers show high electrical conductivity and mechanical performance. By choosing suitable intercalants, air and thermally stable compounds can be obtained. These compounds are applicable for practical application as a light weight conductor in plastic composites. In the present paper, the preparation and electrical properties of bromine intercalated vapor-grown carbon fibers having air and thermal stability are shown, and the electronic structure giving rise to the high conductivity is discussed.

articleTitle: Development of watertree retardant XLPE cables
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: XLPE-insulated medium voltage cables find increasing use due to the good service experience gained. The knowledge that watertreeing (WT) may adversely influence the performance of such cables resulted in activities towards im provements, with special emphasis on developing insulating materials less susceptible to WT. In this paper, development and testing of a new watertree retardant (WTR) XLPE insulating material in MV cables are outlined. The de velopment has resulted in a WTR XLPE cable comparing favorably with standard cables in most respects, while at the same time showing a vastly improved re sistance to watertree formation.

articleTitle: Behaviour of a uniaxially orientated polyethylene tape/oil insulating system under electrical and thermal stresses
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: A uniaxially orientated polyethylene (DOPE) tape has been used for the present series of experiments. A series of experiments were conducted into the effect of electrical and thermal stresses on the tape.

articleTitle: Feature extraction of treeing by image processing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: In this paper, a system to automatically measure tree degradation phenomena in organic insulating materials using an optical microscope is discussed. Using a videographic processing technique, tree features immediately after tree initiation, as well as changes in the configuration of the tree were measured, which up to now have been extremely difficult to observe by conventional visual methods. Cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) was used as, the sample material. A high alternating current voltage was applied, and a long terra breakdown test was conducted. A video camera was used for visual measurement, and a personal computer was used for the image processing, of the tree. As a result, it was possible to record the tree image, and to describe the tree growth, degraded area of tree, the sequential image of the tree and the feature extraction in the thinned image.

articleTitle: Combustion properties of cable-covering materials
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: It is known that polyolefin compounds filled with carbon black show flame retardant properties; however, the mechanism of improvement in these proper ties has not been determined.(1)(2) We investigated the flame-retardant proper ties and thermal properties of carbon black-filled polyolefins and discovered that remarkable improvement in flame-retardant property, especially in the region where carbon black content was small, is mainly due to the pyrolysis inhibition of the polyolefin rather than the oxidation restriction in the burning process.

articleTitle: Photocurrent and thermally stimulated currents in epoxy-alumina composites I
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: Photocurrent and TSC measurements were carried out on epoxy-alumina composites. The photocurrent in the composites was almost equal to that in epoxy resin and showed remarkable dependence on the polarity of the applied field. This suggested that holes were more mobile than electrons in the composites such as epoxy resin and alumina. The elec tronic carriers generated by illumination could pass through the epoxy alumina interface and move in the alumina bulk. Some of the carriers were trapped at the epoxy-alumina interface, or in the alumina bulk or the epoxy bulk near the interface and gave rise to new TSC peaks.

articleTitle: Breakdown propagation velocity in polyethylene applied nano-second rectangular high voltage
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: The time to electrical breakdown in polyethylene for point-to-plane gap configuration has been studied using a photo optical current measuring technique and a 760 nano-second rectangular high-voltage pulse generator. The measured relation between breakdown time lag and gap spacing has been used to deduce the breakdown propagation velocity in the solid studied. The velocities deduced for a positive 5OkV and negative 6OkV point voltage are 1.7km/s and 0.38km/s, respectively.

articleTitle: The temperature dependence of charge decay in E-beam-irradiated pmma using a pulsed electroacoustic method
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: The spatial electric charge distribution in insulating materials irradiated by a 1MeV electron beam was measured using a pulsed electroacoustic method. We observed the dependence of the deformity of the charge distribution profile and the decay of the total accumulated charges in polymethylmethacrylate(PMMA) at various temperatures.

articleTitle: A knowledge representation for insulation diagnosis
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: We discussed how to select a better from of knowledge representation which establishes the optimum expert system for insulation diagnosis. For the insulation diagnosis of electrical equipment, we couldproduce an better expert system in which diagnostic methods were systematically classified in the form of a table and heuristic knowledge is designated by rules.

articleTitle: Electrical conduction properties of N/sup +/ ion implanted low density polyethylene films
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: Surface and bulk conduction properties have been measured in low density polyethylene(LDPE), after N/sup +/ion bombardment, in the ion dose range af 10/sup 14/-10/sup 16/ ions/cm 2. The beams used are 30keV and the film thickness of LDPE is 30/spl mu/m:. The surface resistivity of the films changes by 9 orders of magnitude from its nonirradiated value of 5x10/sup 17//spl Omega// to 2x10/sup //spl Omega// at a dose of 10/sup 16/cm/sup -2/. The bulk c6nductivity increases with increasing the dose, and considerable asymmetry in the current-voltage(I-V) characteristics appears at an ion dose of 10/sup 16/cm/sup -2/. The rectifying ratio is 4 orders of magnitude.

articleTitle: Study on the dielectric system for oil-free 6kV power capacitors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: The use of an oil-free design for 6kV power capacitors has not been realized previously, primarily from an economical point of view. Recently, however, the oil-free design is strongly recom mended for service entrance equipment in buildings and underground commercial facilities from the standpoint of fire prevention. Two insulation systems are feasible for the production of oil free power capacitors, a molded insulation system or a gas insulation system. Based on the resistance to thermal cycling, economy, and ease of handling, we selected the gas insulation system. This paper reports the results of various tests performed to select a dielectric system for high-voltage gas-insulated capacitors. A possible dielectric system for gas-insulated capacitors was considered to be one of the following: 1. CF-type capacitor; A roll of polypropylene (PP) film and alu minum foil, or 2. MF-type capacitor; A roll of metallized PP film.

articleTitle: The computer simulation for the number of aging ovens in relation to the number of thermal endurance test subscriptions
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: In the case of the thermal endurance test, the majority of the time is consumed by the process of accelerated aging in the oven. Therefore, at the begining of the work for the thermal endurance test in which a great many subscriptions are anticipated, the necessary number of ovens should be estimated for efficient utilization, because this estimation gives some measure of capital investment, running cost and earnings. To acccomplish this purpose, the wait-line model based on The Monte Carlo Method was used. To verify the estimation, a conception of a simplified computing process and many factors based on past records, the probability distribution of subscriptions, average values of aging time at each temperature, variance of the regression line of Arrheniuss plots and periods for preparation and repair for using oven were required.

articleTitle: Radiation damage of ethylene-propylene rubber vulcanizates
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: Several types of EPR vulcanizates without fillers were irradiated by Y ray at room temperature. Mechanical properties, chemical stress relaxation, volume resistivity and chemiluminescence were measured to obtain the relationship between the molecular structure of irradiated EPR and the changes in the properties.

articleTitle: High pressure and thermo depolarization currents for the study of low voltage capacitors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: Taking into account the hypothesis according to which partial discharges are at the origin of corrosion, we studied the capacitance evolution of capacitors placed inside a high pressure chamber. This shows metallization removal with a capacitance drop of 2 % after 1000 hours under 80 x 10/sup 5/ Pa. No partial discharge is detected during the aging time. On the other hand, thermo depolarization currents on capacitor are shown as a technique to test parcels of components.

articleTitle: Separating discharges in film/roller system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: Light, powder figures and electrical magnitude are measured for the dis charges that occur when a charged PET sheet (with and without silicone coating) is separated from a grounded metal cylinder. The characteristics depend upon the polarity and level of the electrification.

articleTitle: The correlation between properties and structure of ethylene-vinyl-acetate (EVA) copolymers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: The structure of ethylene-vinyl-acetate (EVA) copolymers depends strongly on the comp9sition of E (ethylene) and VA (vinyl-acetate). With various compositions in VA:E ratio in weight, the results show that both the density and the melt index increase, while the molecular weight, the melt viscosity and the degree of crystallinity decrease with increasing VA:E ratio in EVA copolymers. This reflects that both the ethylene sequence length and the activation energy of fluidity decrease with increasing VA content. The change of the structure of EVA copolymers is directly correlated with the change of the mechanical and dielectric properties of this material. The peak values of the dielectric constant and the dielectric loss in the dielectric relaxation temperature characteristics increase, while the activation energy of polarization and the dielectric breakdown strength decrease with increasing VA:E ratio. Other mechanical properties, such as the tensile strength and the environment stress cracking, also correspondingly decrease as the molecular weight and the ethylene sequence length decrease due to the increase of VA content in EVA copolymers.

articleTitle: Influence of attachment of insulating string on AC flashover strength of insulator
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: The relation between ac flashover voltage (ACFOV) and an attachment of nylon string on the insulator surface is studied in air by using a PMMA insulator which has a backside electrode. The measurements show that the ACFOV is decreased by the attachment of the string. ACFOV characteristics can be classified into two types with the contact angle between the H.V. electrode and the insulator surface. In a region of the contact angle from 90/spl deg/ to 120/spl deg/, the maximum percentage of the decrease is 15%. In the other region of the angle from 120/spl deg/ to 180/spl deg/, the maximum decrease is 25%.

articleTitle: High-field conduction and breakdown strength in poly-p-xylylene thin film
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: It was shown experimentally that high-field currents in poly-p-xylylene (PPX) films prepared by vacuum pyrolysis(l) were enhanced by collision ionization. In poly-2-chloro-p-xylylene (PCPX) films containing a chlorine atom in a monomer unit of PPX, the high-field current and EL were suppressed in the low temperature region. Similar phenomena were observed on PFX films treated by RF plasma (plasma-treated PPX: P-PPX). These films showed a higher breakdown strength than PPX films. Chlorine atoms or defects intro duced by the plasma treatment were concluded to act as scattering centers and suppress the collision ionizations.

Index Terms: Breast Imaging Reporting And Data System

articleTitle: Breakdown strength of plasma polymer films synthesized from trifluoro-methane and ethylene
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: Electrical breakdown field of plasma polymer films was studied by applying rectangular voltage pulses. The breakdown field increases by the incorpora tion of fluorine atoms into the film when the pulse width is shorter than 5/spl mu/s. This is due to the scattering of electronic carriers caused by C-F bonds.

articleTitle: Electric breakdown and electroluminescence in tantalum pentoxide films
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: As the breakdown of dielectric thin films subjected to high electric fields is the ultimate stage in the lifespan of devices, further information on the breakdown mechanism is very important in the development of high-quality electronic devices and integrated circuits. In this study, electrical breakdown and electroluminescence in anodic Ta/sub 2/O/sub 5/ thin films have been measured. No explicit dependences on thickness and temperature in dielectric breakdown have been observed in these films. Therefore it is difficult to determine the mechanism whether it is electronic or thermal. Also, an attempt has been made to investigate the basic process of electrical breakdown from an optical point of view in the prebreakdown field.

articleTitle: Dielectric polarizability of organic liquids subjected to high pressures
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: The variation of pressure as a means of changing density without affecting temperature is valuable when assessing the validity of expressions for /spl epsilon/(p,T). Examples of both polar and nonpolar liquids are considered.

articleTitle: Electrical properties of mim and mis structures with Langmuir-Blodgett poly diacetylene films
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: Electrical properties are investigated for metal-insulator-metal (MIM) and metal-insulator-semiconductor (MIS) structures with Langmuir-Blodgett poly diacetylene (LB PDA) insulators. Capacitance-voltage (C-V) characteristics are measured for the Al / LB PDA / p-Si (MIS) devices. The C-V curves show hysteresis, and flat-band voltage shifts are observed under the application of bias voltages. These results show charge injection from Si into the MIS devices. Thermally stimulated currents (TSCs) are measured for Al / LB PDA / Al (MIM) structures. TSC peaks caused by dipole polarization and charge injection are observed in the low and in the high temperature regions, re spectively.Furthermore, remarkable change of TSC curves is observed for this structures between before and after annealing.

articleTitle: Automatic measurements of complex permittivity and precise analysis of results
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the Twenty-First Symposium on Electrical Insulating Materials
abstract: Permittivity measurements usinq resonant cavity techniques have been the subject of numerous studies over the past forty years. Conventional cavity perturbation measurements normally use a transmission cavity, sweeper, power detector and an oscilloscope or other instrument to record the resonance curve and thereby provide the necessary information on the resonant frequency and the 0 factor to calculate the permittivity of a sample material placed within the cavity.
